details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

fzf.description: fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, trigger-driven zsh completion in shell/completion.zsh uses _fzf_feed_fifo to create a FIFO at the predictable shared path ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fzf-complete-fifo-$$ and continues after removal or creation errors. On a multi-user host, a local attacker can pre-create that path as a symlink so the victim's completion stream overwrites a victim-writable file, potentially enabling code execution when that file is later sourced. A pre-created FIFO can instead disclose a bounded stream of completion candidates or block completion. On default modern hosts, fs.protected_symlinks blocks the overwrite variant, and protected_fifos and protected_regular further limit the FIFO disclosure and blocking variants, so exploitation depends on the relevant kernel protections being disabled and on the victim invoking the affected completion. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

fzf is a command-line fuzzy finder. Prior to 0.74.5, bin/fzf-tmux validates separately supplied layout sizes but does not validate attached -l and -u layout values before Bash arithmetic expansion, allowing command substitution in a crafted operand to execute as the invoking user during option parsing. The same validation failure lets space-bearing popup geometry options -x, -y, -w, -h, and -p reach an unquoted tmux popup option string and inject additional tmux flags. Exploitation requires less-trusted project configuration, a wrapper, or a plugin to supply the poisoned value and requires the victim to invoke fzf-tmux; normal values are usually trusted, and the script has been superseded by built-in tmux options. This issue is fixed in version 0.74.5.

pylint.description: Pylint is a static code analyser for Python. From 0.15.2 until 4.0.9, Pylint stores module statistics in predictable files under PYLINT_HOME and loads those files with pickle.load on a later run. An attacker who can write to a shared, group-writable, or otherwise untrusted cache directory can replace a stats cache with crafted serialized data, causing arbitrary code to execute with the privileges of the user who next runs Pylint. The default per-user cache is not normally writable by another user. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.9.

cna.title: Kernel: netfilter: race condition between ipset_cmd_add and ipset_cmd_swap

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem of the Linux kernel. A race condition between IPSET_CMD_ADD and IPSET_CMD_SWAP can lead to a kernel panic due to the invocation of `__ip_set_put` on a wrong `set`. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system.

cna.title: Kernel: rsvp: out-of-bounds read in rsvp_classify()

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the IPv4 Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) classifier in the Linux kernel. The xprt pointer may go beyond the linear part of the skb, leading to an out-of-bounds read in the `rsvp_classify` function. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system and cause a denial of service.

workarounds.value: This flaw can be mitigated by preventing the affected `cls_rsvp` kernel module from being loaded. For instructions on how to blacklist a kernel module, please see https://access.redhat.com/solutions/41278.

cna.title: Kernel: ipv4: null pointer dereference in ipv4_send_dest_unreach()

The socket buffer (skb) was assumed to be associated with a device before calling __ip_options_compile, which is not always the case if the skb is re-routed by ipvs. This issue may allow a local user with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to crash the system.

cna.title: Samba: "rpcecho" development server allows denial of service via sleep() call on ad dc

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was found in Samba's "rpcecho" development server, a non-Windows RPC server used to test Samba's DCE/RPC stack elements. This vulnerability stems from an RPC function that can be blocked indefinitely. The issue arises because the "rpcecho" service operates with only one worker in the main RPC task, allowing calls to the "rpcecho" server to be blocked for a specified time, causing service disruptions. This disruption is triggered by a "sleep()" call in the "dcesrv_echo_TestSleep()" function under specific conditions. Authenticated users or attackers can exploit this vulnerability to make calls to the "rpcecho" server, requesting it to block for a specified duration, effectively disrupting most services and leading to a complete denial of service on the AD DC. The DoS affects all other services as "rpcecho" runs in the main RPC task.

cna.title: Satellite: arithmetic overflow in satellite

descriptions.value: An arithmetic overflow flaw was found in Satellite when creating a new personal access token. This flaw allows an attacker who uses this arithmetic overflow to create personal access tokens that are valid indefinitely, resulting in damage to the system's integrity.

cna.title: Kernel: exfat: stack overflow in exfat_get_uniname_from_ext_entry

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the exFAT driver of the Linux kernel. The vulnerability exists in the implementation of the file name reconstruction function, which is responsible for reading file name entries from a directory index and merging file name parts belonging to one file into a single long file name. Since the file name characters are copied into a stack variable, a local privileged attacker could use this flaw to overflow the kernel stack.

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Maxim Suhanov for reporting this issue.

cna.title: Kernel: cxgb4: use-after-free in ch_flower_stats_cb()

descriptions.value: A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the cxgb4 driver in the Linux kernel. The bug occurs when the cxgb4 device is detaching due to a possible rearming of the flower_stats_timer from the work queue. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system, causing a denial of service condition.

cna.title: Samba: smb clients can truncate files with read-only permissions

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was discovered in Samba, where the flaw allows SMB clients to truncate files, even with read-only permissions when the Samba VFS module "acl_xattr" is configured with "acl_xattr:ignore system acls = yes". The SMB protocol allows opening files when the client requests read-only access but then implicitly truncates the opened file to 0 bytes if the client specifies a separate OVERWRITE create disposition request. The issue arises in configurations that bypass kernel file system permissions checks, relying solely on Samba's permissions.

cna.title: ezdxf through 1.4.5 Code Injection via dxf2code DXF Table Entry Names

descriptions.value: ezdxf through 1.4.5 contains a code injection vulnerability in the dxf2code add-on that allows attackers to inject Python code via unescaped single quotes in DXF table entry names. Attackers can craft a DXF file whose layer, linetype, style, or appid names break out of quoted strings in generated scripts, executing code with the privileges of the user running them.

descriptions.description: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

cna.title: torchvision before 0.29.2 Path Traversal via Tar Archive Extraction

descriptions.value: torchvision before 0.29.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in _extract_tar() that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction directory by supplying crafted tar archives. Attackers controlling archives passed to extract_archive() or download_and_extract_archive() can use .. paths, absolute paths, or symlinks to overwrite Python modules and achieve code execution.

descriptions.description: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: torchvision before 0.29.2 Path Traversal via Tar Archive Extraction

cna.title: pyfda through 0.9.5 Code Execution via Insecure Deserialization in load_filter()

descriptions.value: pyfda through 0.9.5 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_filter() that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .npz or .pkl filter files. Attackers can embed a __reduce__ gadget that runs via np.load with allow_pickle=True or pickle.load before validation, executing code with the user's privileges.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: pyfda through 0.9.5 Code Execution via Insecure Deserialization in load_filter()

cna.title: JAL through 2026.11.3 Arbitrary File Overwrite via Symlink in Backup Archive

descriptions.value: JAL (Just Another Ledger) through 2026.11.3 contains an arbitrary file overwrite vulnerability in backup restore that allows attackers to write files by supplying a crafted .tgz backup with a symlink member. Attackers can include a jal.sqlite symlink to an absolute path followed by a regular jal.sqlite member, overwriting files such as shell startup scripts for code execution.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: JAL through 2026.11.3 Arbitrary File Overwrite via Symlink in Backup Archive

cna.title: lastversion before 3.6.20 Arbitrary File Write via Tar Symlink Members

descriptions.value: lastversion before 3.6.20 contains a path traversal vulnerability in extract_tar() that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction directory via tar symlink members. Attackers controlling a project's release assets can craft a tarball with a symlink followed by a file beneath it, writing files like usercustomize.py to achieve code execution.

descriptions.description: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: lastversion before 3.6.20 Arbitrary File Write via Tar Symlink Members

cna.title: LibreChat 0.7.6 before 0.8.8 Denial of Service via Conversation Import

descriptions.value: LibreChat 0.7.6 before 0.8.8 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to block the server event loop by uploading a crafted conversation import file to POST /api/convos/import. Attackers can submit many messages with unresolvable parentMessageId values, triggering quadratic processing in cloneMessagesWithTimestamps or adjustTimestampsForOrdering and stalling the Node.js event loop for minutes for all users.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: LibreChat 0.7.6 before 0.8.8 Denial of Service via Conversation Import

cna.title: Video Popup Block by WPZOOM 1.1.2 before 1.1.9 Stored XSS via Video URL

descriptions.value: Video Popup Block by WPZOOM 1.1.2 before 1.1.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows Contributor-level users to inject markup via unescaped video URL and popup width values. Attackers can store a block whose .mp4 URL or width breaks out of attributes in frontend.js, executing script in the site's origin when users open the popup.

descriptions.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Video Popup Block by WPZOOM 1.1.2 before 1.1.9 Stored XSS via Video URL

cna.title: LibreChat 0.7.8 before 0.8.9 Race Condition in Balance Auto-Refill

descriptions.value: LibreChat 0.7.8 before 0.8.9 contains a race condition vulnerability in checkBalance that allows authenticated users to obtain multiple auto-refill credits by sending concurrent requests. Attackers can send simultaneous chat requests that each pass the unlocked lastRefill check, receiving repeated refillAmount credits and bypassing configured token credit limits.

descriptions.description: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: LibreChat 0.7.8 before 0.8.9 Race Condition in Balance Auto-Refill

cna.title: InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 Memory Exhaustion via /distserve/connection_warmup

descriptions.value: InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 contains an unbounded resource allocation vulnerability in the DistServe proxy /distserve/connection_warmup endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory. While a prefill/decode connection is pending, for example after registering a slow node via /nodes/add, repeated warmup requests spawn unbounded wait_for_conn() tasks and sockets until the proxy process is killed.

descriptions.description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 Memory Exhaustion via /distserve/connection_warmup

cna.title: Foreman: host ssh key not being checked in remote execution

descriptions.value: A vulnerability was found in Satellite. When running a remote execution job on a host, the host's SSH key is not being checked. When the key changes, the Satellite still connects it because it uses "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no". This flaw can lead to a man-in-the-middle attack (MITM), denial of service, leaking of secrets the remote execution job contains, or other issues that may arise from the attacker's ability to forge an SSH key. This issue does not directly allow unauthorized remote execution on the Satellite, although it can leak secrets that may lead to it.
